title: The OWASP Top 10:2025 and the API Top 10
summary: The ten categories security teams, scanners and auditors use, what changed since 2021, the API list's highlights, and the newest category: failing open when something goes wrong.

steps.title: The OWASP Top 10:2025
body: OWASP's Top 10 is the shared vocabulary of web security: pentest reports, scanner findings, audits and job interviews use its ids. The current edition is **2025** (the eighth), built from data on millions of tested applications:
| Id | Category | You meet it as |
| A01 | **Broken Access Control** | another user's order by changing an id; SSRF; CSRF; path traversal |
| A02 | **Security Misconfiguration** | stack traces in production, default passwords, missing headers, open storage |
| A03 | **Software Supply Chain Failures** | a vulnerable or malicious package, a compromised build |
| A04 | **Cryptographic Failures** | unsalted fast password hashes, no TLS, home-made crypto |
| A05 | **Injection** | SQL, OS commands, LDAP, and cross-site scripting (XSS) |
| A06 | **Insecure Design** | a checkout that trusts the client's price |
| A07 | **Authentication Failures** | no rate limit on login, session fixation, weak recovery |
| A08 | **Software or Data Integrity Failures** | unsigned updates, unsafe deserialization |
| A09 | **Security Logging and Alerting Failures** | the attack happened and nobody was told |
| A10 | **Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions** | an error path that lets the request through |

**What changed since 2021:** SSRF is no longer its own category (it is part of A01). *Vulnerable and Outdated Components* grew into **A03 Software Supply Chain Failures** (build systems and distribution too). **A10** is new. Security Misconfiguration rose from 5th to 2nd. XSS has been part of Injection since 2021.

steps.prompt: Match each finding from a pentest report to its OWASP Top 10:2025 category.
pairs: `?q=' UNION SELECT ... FROM users--` dumps the users table
The production error page shows a stack trace and the SQL
Passwords are stored as unsalted SHA-256
A build pulled a typo-squatted npm package

steps.title: The API Security Top 10 (2023)
body: APIs get their own list. Its 2023 edition is still current. The ones you will meet most:
- **API1 Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)**: the IDOR above. First on the list since the first edition.
- **API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization**: reading fields you should not (over-exposure) or writing them (mass assignment: `{"isAdmin": true}`).
- **API5 Broken Function Level Authorization**: a customer can call `POST /admin/refunds`.
- **API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption**: no rate limits, no page size cap, no upload size limit.

- **API7 SSRF**, **API8 Security Misconfiguration**, **API9 Improper Inventory Management** (the forgotten `/v1` without the fixes), **API10 Unsafe Consumption of APIs** (trusting what a partner's API sends you).

Authorization appears three times. Authentication (who are you?) is rarely the problem in modern APIs; *what may you do, to which object, with which fields* is. The **Authentication & JWT** topic covers BOLA in its API security module; this topic exploits and fixes it in a live app.

steps.prompt: File each finding under its OWASP Top 10:2025 category.
items: A support link makes the admin's browser change their email address
A review containing `<script>` runs in other users' browsers
`?host=127.0.0.1; id` on a ping tool prints `uid=`
10,000 password guesses a minute are answered without delay
The session id stays the same before and after sign-in
steps.explain: SSRF and CSRF both count as broken access control in 2025: the attacker borrows someone else's access (the server's network position, the victim's session). Default credentials are filed under misconfiguration because the fix is a setting.

steps.prompt: Your team's 2021-era checklist has a line "A10:2021 Server-Side Request Forgery". Where does SSRF sit in the 2025 edition?
options: It was dropped: modern frameworks prevent it
steps.explain: SSRF was merged into Broken Access Control; A10:2025 is now Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions. Update the checklist ids, not the checks: SSRF is as common as ever in cloud apps.

steps.title: A10: when the error path lets everyone in
body: A10:2025 is about what code does when something unexpected happens: a timeout, a null, a parse error, a full disk. The dangerous version is **failing open**: the safety check could not run, so the request goes through.
```csharp fragment
bool allowed;
try
allowed = amount <= limits.ForUser(user);   // a call to the limits service
catch (Exception)
allowed = true;   // "don't block support staff when the limits service is down"

An attacker who can make the limits service slow (a flood of requests, a huge input) now has no limit at all. **Fail closed**: when a security decision cannot be made, the answer is no. Log the error, alert on it, and show the user a clear "try again later". Availability problems are visible and get fixed; silent fail-open holes get exploited.

steps.prompt: The limits service times out. What does this print?
steps.explain: Fail-open approves a 5000 refund nobody checked. Fail-closed refuses it, and still approves normal refunds when the service answers.

steps.title: Fail closed on refunds
prompt: Support staff issue refunds. `CanRefund` asks `limitLookup(user)` for the user's limit, which calls a service that sometimes times out or fails. Fix it:
- a refund of 0 or less is refused (a negative refund is a charge);
- a refund above the limit is refused; up to and including the limit is allowed.
Keep the signature: `bool CanRefund(string user, decimal amount, Func<string, decimal> limitLookup)`.
starter: bool CanRefund(string user, decimal amount, Func<string, decimal> limitLookup)
return true; // don't block support staff when the limits service is down
solution: bool CanRefund(string user, decimal amount, Func<string, decimal> limitLookup)
// Fail closed: no decision means no. (Log and alert here in a real service.)
hints: In the `catch`, the safe answer is `false`.
Check `amount <= 0` before anything else and return `false`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a 50 refund within sam's 100 limit is allowed", true, CanRefund("sam", 50m, limits));
Dojo.Eq("exactly the limit is allowed", true, CanRefund("sam", 100m, limits));
Dojo.Eq("100.01 is over the limit", false, CanRefund("sam", 100.01m, limits));
Dojo.Eq("another user's lower limit applies", false, CanRefund("kim", 50m, limits));
Dojo.Eq("a timeout from the limits service refuses", false, CanRefund("sam", 50m, _ => throw new TimeoutException()));
Dojo.Eq("any other failure refuses too", false, CanRefund("sam", 5m, _ => throw new InvalidOperationException("503 from the limits service")));
Dojo.Eq("a negative refund is refused", false, CanRefund("sam", -10m, limits));
Dojo.Eq("a zero refund is refused", false, CanRefund("sam", 0m, limits));
